newsitem.title: USA: Environmentalists applaud Antarctica law signing.
newsitem.headline: Environmentalists applaud Antarctica law signing.

text.p: Environmental groups on Wednesday applauded President Bill Clinton's signing of a law to carry out the United States' responsibilities under an international treaty to protect Antarctica's environment.

"We challenge Russia, Japan and Finland to follow the lead of the United States by completing their ratification so this important environmental agreement can take effect," Gerald Leape, a biodiversity campaigner for Greenpeace, said in a statement.
Twenty-six nations active in Antarctica signed the treaty but the three countries have not yet ratified it.
The bill makes U.S. research activities consistent with the treaty, imposes strict rules on burning or disposing of waste, and continues the ban on exploration and development of Antarctic minerals.

"For the first time explorers and researchers who study life on the edge will have to stop and think before they act," Beth Marks Clark, president of the Antarctica Project environmental group, said in a statement.
Under the law, all visitors are obligated to diminish any potential harm they may have on the fragile Antarctic environment.
